title: Design System: Express Photo and Gifts

blue.note: Binding brand value, supplied by the shop. Owns cover, running band and find-us whole. Takes white text.

blue-lift.note: Hover state for the blue action only; not a surface colour.

gold.note: The shop's highlighter. Pairs legibly with ink or brand blue; never takes white text; never a region's background.

leather.note: Same value as brand blue, named for its role as a ground so a surface and an accent are not confused at call sites.

leather-deep.note: The darkest stop in the cover scrim, and the only place it appears.

card.note: Closes the page: collect-or-deliver and the footer.

paper.note: Body ground, the gifting reading surface, and the translucent header's base.

paper-deep.note: The shelf's trough, ruled top and bottom; also the scrollbar track.

print.note: Shelf cards, the photographs' own backing, the skip link.

ink.note: Body text on paper, and the label on amber.

ink-soft.note: Secondary prose on paper. Blue-leaning, never grey.

ink-faint.note: The quietest tone on paper: index numbers, the shelf hint, the occasions label, the placeholder note.

on-leather-soft.note: Ledes, hours values and contact glyphs on blue.

rule-paper.note: The hairline that separates ledger rows, card bodies and the shelf's edges on paper.

rule-leather.note: The hairline on blue and near-black grounds.

display.purpose: The cover headline only, two lines, lower-left.

band.purpose: The running word band — one weight lighter than a headline so a moving line does not out-shout a fixed one.

statement.purpose: The highlighter-marked line; the only prose that takes the amber stroke.

subtitle.purpose: Collect-or-deliver headings, set inline with their icon.

cover-lede.purpose: The one sentence under the display line, capped at 58ch.

address.purpose: The street address block on blue.

lede.purpose: Section-opening prose, capped at the 62ch measure.

drawer-link.purpose: Mobile navigation links in the paper drawer.

button.purpose: Pill action labels; 13.5px in the compact header variant.

body.purpose: Fulfilment paragraphs, contact rows, hours day labels.

body-sm.purpose: Ledger blurbs, footer lists and blurb, the fulfilment note.

micro.purpose: Compact header nav and actions, the shelf placeholder note.

mark.purpose: Mono section marks, the scroll cue and shop block headings. Uppercase, tracked 0.16em.

slot.purpose: The reserved action slot on every ledger row, and the footer base line.

colophon.purpose: The footer phone number in amber mono.

shadows.name: action-gold
shadows.purpose: Under the amber primary action at rest.

shadows.name: action-gold-hover
shadows.purpose: The amber action on hover, paired with a 2px lift.

shadows.name: action-blue
shadows.purpose: Under the blue action on paper.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The shelf card at rest; the only container shadow in the system.

shadows.name: card-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: The shelf card raised 4px on hover.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only CSS easing in the system: button lifts, card lifts and shadow transitions.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active state on every pill action.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover on every button variant; 4px over 0.5s on the shelf card.

motion.name: gsap-entrance
motion.value: gsap.from({ y: 26, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 1, ease: 'expo.out', stagger: 0.09 })
motion.purpose: The cover's entrance — headline, lede, actions, cue.

motion.name: gsap-reveal
motion.value: ScrollTrigger.batch('[data-reveal]', { start: 'top 88%', once: true }) -> gsap.from({ y: 30, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.9, ease: 'expo.out', stagger: 0.08 })
motion.purpose: The one reveal grammar for sections; shelf cards use y: 40 / 0.8s / 0.07 at 'top 92%'.

motion.name: gsap-wall
motion.value: rows at 58s / 74s / 46s linear, alternate rows reversed, xPercent 0 <-> -50; wall scrubbed 0.6 to yPercent 12, scale 1.06
motion.purpose: The three-speed cover wall and its scroll-linked drift.

motion.name: gsap-band
motion.purpose: The running word band's loop; the run is duplicated so the seam is invisible.

motion.name: gsap-marked
motion.purpose: The highlighter stroke drawing itself in as the marked line arrives.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: gsap.matchMedia() returns before any tween is created; CSS collapses animation/transition to 0.001ms
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion is answered before motion exists, not by reverting it afterwards.

focusRings.name: on-dark
focusRings.purpose: Inside .on-dark; brand blue is invisible against a blue ground.

focusRings.name: on-gold
focusRings.purpose: On the amber action, where both blue and gold lose contrast.

narrative.overview:
This is a printed shop, not an app. The argument is the shop's own work: the first thing a visitor meets is a full-bleed wall of real product photographs travelling past behind one plain sentence, and from there the page reads the way the counter reads — a numbered ledger of the four services, a running band of everything the shop turns out, one shelf of things to look at, then where to find the door. Deep brand blue owns the loud surfaces whole; warm paper owns the surfaces you read on; near-black closes the page. Nothing is quiet for the sake of being quiet.

The density is deliberate and left-weighted: display type sits low-left at large clamped sizes with tight negative tracking, ledger rows are ruled hairlines rather than boxes, and long prose is capped at a 62ch measure so a wide shell never turns into a wide paragraph. Depth is low and warm — pill actions carry a coloured glow rather than a grey drop shadow, the one card has a single soft blue-tinted lift, and everything else earns separation from its ground instead of from a shadow.

The system has one accent and uses it like a highlighter, not like a second brand colour. Amber marks the action to take and the line worth remembering; it never becomes a region. There is no dark variant — color-scheme: light is declared, and the dark surfaces are compositional grounds, not a theme. The confirmed rejection is the previous build's sparse gallery treatment: the failure there was under-spending the material, not choosing the wrong material.
keyCharacteristics: Four grounds in rotation: brand blue (loud), warm paper and deeper paper (reading), near-black (close).
Amber as the shop's highlighter — actions, one marked line, band slashes, marks on dark; never a region's background.
Two families, strictly divided: Archivo for prose, Geist Mono for marks and measurements only.
Pill actions (999px), 12/18/22px surface radii, one soft blue-tinted elevation.
A load-bearing cover scrim that turns a wall of white-ground studio photographs into a single readable surface.
Focus rings that change colour with their ground.
Motion animates from an already-visible default; with JS off the page is complete and merely still.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Amber marks; it does not upholster. It may carry a button, a line of text, a slash, a mark, a chip, an underline or a marker glyph — it may never be the background of a whole region, a section, a card or a hero. Audit test: if you can point at an amber area larger than a button, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Whole-Ground Rule
rules.body: A ground owns its section edge to edge. Blue, paper, deeper paper and night card alternate as full-bleed bands; a coloured panel floating inside a differently-coloured section is not part of this world.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from its ground's hue — blue-leaning on paper, periwinkle on blue, cool slate on near-black. There is no grey in this palette.

rules.name: The Two-Families Rule
rules.body: Archivo sets everything written in prose. Geist Mono sets only marks and measurements — section marks, index numbers, the reserved slot, hours, the shelf hint, the footer colophon. Mono is never body copy, never a heading, never a button. Audit test: read the mono string aloud; if it is a sentence, it is in the wrong family.

rules.name: The Tight-Display Rule
rules.body: The larger the type, the tighter it sets: -0.035em and 0.94 line-height at display, -0.03em at headline, normal tracking by the time it is prose. Never letterspace Archivo positively; positive tracking (0.16em) belongs to mono alone.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped — 62ch for ledes, 58ch on the cover, 48ch for ledger blurbs, 44ch for fulfilment paragraphs, 36ch in the footer — regardless of how wide the 1400px shell gets.

rules.name: The One-Edge Rule
rules.body: Every band re-applies the shell and gutter. A full-bleed background never means full-bleed content.

rules.name: The Coloured-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is tinted by the thing casting it — amber under the amber button, brand blue under the blue button and the white card. Black or neutral-grey shadows are not part of this world.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Lists, ledgers and tables are separated by 1px hairlines, not by borders around each item. The shelf card is the only bordered container on the page.

rules.name: The Two-Shape Rule
rules.body: Pill or soft rectangle. A square corner, a half-round squircle or a radius outside 12/18/22/999 is outside the system.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: The cover's 98° left-weighted gradient (rgb(0 15 90 / 0.96) → rgb(0 29 164 / 0.9) at 38% → rgb(0 29 164 / 0.42) at 66% → rgb(0 29 164 / 0.12)) plus its foot scrim (36% tall, rgb(0 17 98 / 0.94) to transparent) is load-bearing, not decoration. Studio product shots are photographed on white; without the scrim the wall is a field of white rectangles and white display type has nothing to sit on. The gradient holds the type side dark enough for white text and releases to near-clear on the right so the work still shows its true colour, and the foot scrim catches the cue and the actions. Do not delete it as 'a gradient', do not flatten it to a uniform overlay, and do not re-balance it without re-checking white type against the lightest photograph in row one.

rules.name: The From-Visible Rule
rules.body: Every tween is a gsap.from off an already-visible default. The markup renders complete; if the script never runs the page is intact and merely still. Nothing may be hidden in CSS and revealed by JS.

rules.name: The Single-Orchestrator Rule
rules.body: New motion goes into the existing matchMedia block, not into a new component effect. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce returns before a single tween is created — not after, and not by reverting them — and the global stylesheet additionally collapses any CSS animation or transition to 0.001ms.

dos: Do let a ground own its section edge to edge — blue for loud, paper / deeper paper for reading, night card to close.
Do spend amber on the action, the marked line, the band slashes, marks on dark, ::marker and ::selection — and stop there.
Do set every mark, index number, reserved slot, hours value and colophon in Geist Mono, and everything readable as a sentence in Archivo.
Do keep the cover scrim as a load-bearing gradient, and re-check white type against the lightest photograph whenever the wall's contents change.

Do tune the focus ring to its ground: brand blue by default, amber inside .on-dark, ink on .on-gold. A single ring colour is invisible on one ground or the other — blue disappears into the blue panels, amber disappears into paper.
Do tint secondary text from its ground's hue (soft ink and faint ink on paper, periwinkle on blue, soft card ink on near-black).
Do rule lists and tables with hairlines, and reserve borders for the shelf card.
Do animate from an already-visible default, inside the one matchMedia block.
Do cap prose at its measure (62ch default) no matter how wide the shell is.
Do draw icons on the 24px grid at 1.6 stroke with round caps, and keep brand marks solid.
donts: Don't make amber the background of a region, section, card or hero. It is a highlighter, not an upholstery.
Don't set body copy, headings or button labels in mono, and don't letterspace Archivo positively.
Don't introduce a radius outside 12 / 18 / 22 / 999px, or square off a corner.
Don't use grey or black shadows; shadows are tinted by what casts them, and only actions and the shelf card cast one.
Don't float a coloured panel inside a differently-coloured section instead of banding the ground.
Don't use a grey neutral for secondary text.
Don't hide content in CSS for a JS reveal to uncover.
Don't ship a dark-mode variant; color-scheme: light is declared and the dark grounds are composition, not theme.
Don't swap Archivo for the template's Outfit or any other default face without a reason no other face could satisfy.
